THIS PROJECT IS NOT RELATED TO SHADPS4. ALL QUESTIONS RELATED TO THIS PROJECT SHOULD BE SENT TO THE DISCORD SERVER https://discord.gg/KYZRKk9CB, NOT TO THE SHADPS4 SERVER.


# bbport — a native Linux port of Bloodborne

**English** · [Русский](README.ru.md)

bbport is the counterpart of Wine + DXVK for a single game: *Bloodborne* for PlayStation 4
(CUSA03173, game version 1.09) on an x86-64 Linux PC. The game's original executable runs
directly on the PC:

- **as in Wine**, the game's x86-64 code runs on the CPU directly, and a runtime written for
  this one game replaces the PS4 system libraries;
- **as in DXVK**, the game's graphics are translated to Vulkan — by the port's own renderer and
  shader translator (they started from [shadPS4](https://github.com/shadps4-emu/shadPS4)'s and were
  rewritten), including temporal upscaling with AMD FSR 3.1, FSR 4, FSR 4.1.1 and NVIDIA DLSS;
- memory and the GPU's work follow the PC model on every GPU by default (the new memory and
  translation model, since 0.6); the old memory model of 0.3 stays as a launcher option
  (*Memory model → Old*).

What remains to the full Wine + DXVK model: removing the old memory model once the new one is
confirmed on NVIDIA and Intel (see below).

> **No game files are included.** You need your own dump of Bloodborne with update 1.09: any retail
> release (CUSA00900 in the US, CUSA03173 for the European Game of the Year edition, ...), as they
> share the same executable.
> This project is not affiliated with Sony Interactive Entertainment, FromSoftware or AMD.

**Status: experimental, playable.** The game boots, loads saves and plays (the Hunter's Dream
and several areas of Yharnam were played with it) with sound, gamepad and saving.
A full play-through has not been verified, and only one machine (Linux, AMD Radeon RX 7800 XT,
Mesa/RADV) has been tested thoroughly.

## Highlights

- **Native execution.** The eboot is converted offline into a flat memory image; PS4 libc and
  libSceFios2 are linked into it as native code. No CPU emulation and no per-instruction
  translation: the game code runs at full speed.
- **Two memory models** (launcher → *Mode → Memory and translation model*; *Auto*, the default,
  is the new one on every GPU):
  - **The new memory and translation model — the default on every GPU (0.6).** The game's memory lives
    in system RAM and the GPU reads it where it is, as a PC game's buffers; data it reads often
    is kept in VRAM and given back when unused (textures after 20 s, buffers after 60 s). The
    layer's memory module tracks CPU writes to mirrored blocks to keep those copies coherent;
    it does not copy the whole GPU-visible memory. The PS4 command processor's work
    is translated into Vulkan commands rather than emulated on the CPU: memory writes
    (`WRITE_DATA`, DMA) are done by the GPU in command-stream order, and fences are written by the
    GPU itself at the end of the pipeline, at the same point of the stream as the PS4's command
    processor writes them. On every GPU the game's memory goes through the layer's memory module:
    bound in place, VRAM copies as separate buffers, no sparse binding (NVIDIA's sparse binding
    froze the GPU for seconds; on AMD the module is faster than the former sparse arena too);
    `BB_LAYER_MEMORY=0` gives AMD's sparse arena. Tested thoroughly on an RX 7800 XT; on NVIDIA
    by testers. A driver that fails the startup checks falls back to VRAM copies by itself.
    Without the launcher: `BB_PC_MODEL=1/0` (unset: the new one, as *Auto*).
  - **The old memory model, as in 0.3** (*Old*). VRAM copies of the game's memory, writes
    tracked through page protection, with every fix made since 0.3.

  [Changes in 0.6](docs/CHANGES_0.6.md), [0.6-pre1](docs/CHANGES_0.6-pre1.md),
  [0.51](docs/CHANGES_0.51.md), [0.5](docs/CHANGES_0.5.md).

  Unused textures are freed in both modes, so VRAM no longer grows with every area visited.
- **Unlocked frame rate.** Hooks in the game's code make the simulation use the real frame time
  (the community patches in `patches/Bloodborne.xml` remain for comparison, `BB_FRAME_HOOKS=0`);
  ~90 FPS at 4K with FSR 4 Balanced on an RX 7800 XT, ~150 FPS at 1440p with FSR 4 Quality.
  Also 30/60/90 FPS modes; **F3** switches a 30 FPS limit on and off while playing (some
  cinematics, e.g. Laurence's, are safest at 30).
- **Any aspect ratio, live.** 4:3, 16:10, 16:9, 21:9 and 32:9 with the HUD at the screen's edges,
  through hooks (the game's code is not patched); cinematics are wide too.
- **Keyboard and mouse.** Mouse look turns the game's camera directly; a mouse pointer in the
  game's menus (F1 releases the mouse); a layout close to Dark Souls III's (Space dodge, Left
  Shift run, Shift+Space jump); movement keys ramp up like a stick; button prompts show the bound
  key, or the buttons of the gamepad in use (Xbox and others), PlayStation icons only with a
  PlayStation pad.
- **Online play and seamless co-op.** Two pools on shadPS4 0.2

# P.T. for PC **A native PC port of P.T., the 2014 PS4 teaser by Kojima Productions. Windows, Linux and macOS.** ![Lisa in the hallway](docs/media/lisa.gif)
> [!IMPORTANT] > **This port is made by one person in their spare time.** If it gave you a good scare, please consider supporting it on [**Patreon**](https://www.patreon.com/loreanxavier). It pays for the testing hardware and keeps the updates coming. > [!NOTE] > **Bug reports:** I've closed GitHub Issues because of ongoing spam attacks. Please join the [Discord server](https://discord.gg/3vKwUf2eTb) to report bugs. This is a native PC port of P.T., the 2014 PS4 teaser by Kojima Productions. It is not an emulator. The game logic was rebuilt in C++ from the original's behaviour, with Vulkan and DirectX 12 renderers; every level, model, texture, sound, script and cutscene is read at run time from your own copy of the PS4 game. There is no game data in this repository and none in the installer. The port runs on its own engine, Hallway Engine. I made this in my spare time, with AI tools (see AI Disclosure at the end), because P.T. deserved to keep existing somewhere other than on consoles that still have it installed. It plays the whole teaser from the first wake-up to the street, with the voice part included. ## What you need - Your own copy of P.T. The port is built and tested with the US release, CUSA01127, as a dump folder from your console or a fake PKG made from that dump. The folder can have any name: the game recognises it by its files. Other releases, such as the European CUSA01114, are accepted the same way, but I have not seen their data myself; the game logs at its start what differs from the US data. A store PKG cannot be used: it is encrypted for the console that owns it, and nothing here decrypts it. - Windows 10 or 11 (x64), Linux x86-64 with glibc 2.38 or newer (Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 13, Fedora 39, current Arch and SteamOS), or macOS 14 or newer on an Apple silicon or Intel Mac. - A GPU and driver with Vulkan 1.3; on macOS the port brings MoltenVK, which runs Vulkan on Metal. The optional ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion and reflections need a GPU with Vulkan ray queries (not on macOS). DLSS needs a GeForce RTX card. Available upscalers depend on the platform and renderer; see docs/upscaling.md. The settings page greys out what your machine cannot run and says why. - A microphone for one part of the game, as on the PS4. If you have none, `key = J` under `[voice]` in `pt.ini` lets a key stand in for the spoken word. ## Installing Download the installer from the Releases page: `P.T.PC.Port.Setup.exe` on Windows, the Linux setup binary on Linux. Point it at your dump folder or fake PKG and at a destination folder (the default on Windows is `%LocalAppData%\Programs\P.T. PC Port`). It copies the three game archives it needs (`chunk1.psarc`, `texture.qar`, `pathid_list_ps4.bin`) next to the port and makes a shortcut if you want one. The eboot, modules and system files are not used. Linux: `chmod +x` the setup and run it from a terminal. The game needs only glibc and the system's Vulkan driver. On a Steam Deck install from desktop mode and add `pt` as a non-Steam game; it runs on SteamOS as it is. macOS: download `P.T.PC.Port-macOS-arm64.zip` (M1 and later) or `P.T.PC.Port-macOS-x64.zip` (Intel), unzip `P.T. PC Port.app`, open it once and allow it under System Settings > Privacy & Security (it is not signed with a Developer ID), then pick your dump folder when it asks. A fake PKG has to be extracted on Windows or Linux first. Intel Macs need a GPU that MoltenVK can run the renderer on; the port was written without a Mac at hand and the Intel app has not been run on one yet. More in docs/macos.md. Windows and Linux releases include installers and portable ZIPs. To update an existing installation, use the game's update button or run the new installer over it. Your game archives, settings, saves and mods stay. On Windows and Linux, settings, saves, logs and cache live in `data/` beside the executable. The game migrates existing user data without overwriting newer files. On macOS, these stay i

# Uncharted: The Nathan Drake Collection for Windows

**Uncharted 1, 2 and 3 from the PS4 collection running natively on Windows 10 and 11, by [SuperMedo](https://github.com/Supermedo).** Mohammed Albarghouthi

Same idea as my [Bloodborne port](https://github.com/Supermedo/bloodborne_pc): the original PS4 game
code runs directly on your PC and the graphics are translated to Vulkan. Unpack the zip, start
`Uncharted.exe`, pick your game folder, choose a game and press **PLAY**.

**[Download the latest version](https://github.com/Supermedo/uncharted_pc/releases/latest)** · **[Join the Discord](https://discord.gg/s3RgH6cRfJ)**

> **No game files are included.** You need your own decrypted dump of the collection
> (CUSA02343, CUSA02320, ...: the folder with eboot.bin, big2-ps4_Shipping.elf,
> big3-ps4_Shipping.elf, sce_sys, u1data, u2data and u3data).
> This project is not affiliated with Sony Interactive Entertainment or Naughty Dog.

## Features

- All three games from one launcher: Drake's Fortune, Among Thieves and Drake's Deception.
- 60 FPS like on PS4, or 120 FPS (higher rates are experimental).
- Render resolution above 1080p (up to 3200x1800) and ultrawide aspect ratios: the games draw a real larger or wider picture, set in the launcher.
- Anti-aliasing with TAA, AMD FSR 3.1, AMD FSR 4 or NVIDIA DLSS (DLAA).
- Frame generation: AMD FSR 3 (any GPU) or NVIDIA DLSS (RTX 40 2x, RTX 50 up to 4x).
- Keyboard, mouse and controller together, all remappable. Mouse look in U3.
- Stereo, 5.1 or 7.1 sound: the games are told the real speaker layout (it follows the Windows setting, or pick it in the launcher).
- Trophies: the games' own trophy lists in the launcher, and a notice in the game when you earn one.
- Button prompts for keyboard and mouse, Xbox or PlayStation controllers; controller vibration settings.
- Cheats page (infinite health and ammo per game), launcher languages, your own covers and Steam art.
- A Fixes page for fixes that cost speed: Automatic turns each one on only where it helps.
- Add to Steam and desktop shortcuts from the launcher, automatic updates.

## Requirements

- Windows 10 (1903 or later) or Windows 11, 64-bit.
- An Intel Core 3rd generation (Ivy Bridge) or newer, an AMD Ryzen, or an AMD FX. Older Intel CPUs
  with AVX (Core 2nd and 3rd generation, Xeon E3 v1/v2): experimental, see Known problems.
- A graphics card with Vulkan 1.3 and a current driver, with **6 GB of video memory or more**.
  4 GB cards (GTX 1650, RX 570) run out of video memory and crash after a while; on those, keep
  Anti-aliasing and Frame generation off.
- About 8 GB of free memory (RAM + page file).

## Known problems

- **Uncharted 3, Cartagena square (chapter 2):** at high frame rates (240 Hz setting, ~80 FPS)
  the game could freeze and close with "GPU crash: the graphics device was lost". It came from
  the speed fix for that area and is fixed in 0.3. If it still happens to you, set Frame rate to
  60 on the Display page and open an issue with your `user\last_run.log`.
- **Uncharted 3:** green or black shapes flashing on Sully's shirt in Cartagena: the cloth
  solvers raced on NVIDIA's 32-lane groups. Fixed in 0.3.9 with BilalReloaded's fix.
- **Crash with "ASSERTION: GetRenderFrameParams(frameToFreeInstancesFor)->m_gfxEopTick"**
  (mostly U1 after the first cutscene): the game expected the GPU side to be done with a frame it
  wanted to reuse, and stopped when it wasn't yet (shaders building on a first run). Fixed in
  0.3.2 (0.3.4 for the 1.02 versions): the game now waits for it. If you still see it, open an
  issue with your log.
- **Intel HD / UHD graphics:** a black screen on the HD 630 is fixed in 0.3.3. Older Intel chips
  (HD 520) can still crash inside Intel's own driver.
- **Uncharted 3 London bar crash** (fault at `0xd9c59b`, or device lost in the bar fight): fixed in
  0.3.4.
- **Uncharted 2 loading crashes** (`ReadSync file (req/read: ...)`, white textures then
  `iSubMesh < m_numSubMeshInstances`): file reads could come back cut short. Fixed in 0.3.5.
- **Older CPUs:** the games use instructions of the PS4's processor (AVX, BMI1, MOVBE, LZCNT).
  Since 0.3.7 they are rewritten on CPUs that lack them, so Intel Core 3rd generation (Ivy Bridge)
  runs, as does AMD FX. Sandy Bridge (2nd generation) also lacks F16C and is not supported.
- **Random crashes with "execute access to 0" or a fault at `0x63f5d0` (U1):** Windows wrote its
  exception data over values the game keeps just below the stack pointer. Fixed in 0.3.7.
- **Uncharted 2, train wreck:** `IsFinite(deltaTransform)` in character-leg-ik.cpp, fixed in 0.3.6
  for the EU 1.00 version.
- Frame rates above 120 are experimental.

## Building

MSYS2 CLANG64 on Windows: `bash build.sh` builds `out\bb-probe.exe`, and
`bash packaging/windows/package.sh` makes `dist\uncharted-windows` and the zip.

## Credits

Built on [bbport](https://github.com/deadinside28/bloodborne_pc), the native Linux port of
Bloodborne by deadinside28, and on the [shadPS4

content.readme:
# USD BRep

Solid modeling for [OpenUSD](https://openusd.org/). USD BRep creates and edits
boundary-representation (BRep) solids and reads and writes them in USD as
`BrepArray` prims.

BRep faces and edges can be NURBS or analytic geometry. Plane, cylinder, cone, sphere
and torus faces are written to USD as analytic surfaces. Edge curves are written as
NURBS; analytic line, circle and ellipse edges in USD from other tools are read as
analytic curves. Other SMLib types, such as parabolas and surfaces of revolution, are
written as NURBS. See [supported geometry](.agents/operations/usd_import_export.md#supported-geometry)
for the SMLib class names.

## Repo contents

### USD

Libraries and tools that work on BReps stored in USD files:

- **[USD BRep schema](source/schema/README.md) (omniSolid):** defines the `BrepArray` prim, which stores BReps in
  USD with their full topology and NURBS or analytic geometry; see the
  [proposal](proposals/UsdSolid/README.md) and its
  [problem statement](proposals/cad_geometry/README.md).
- **[Import/export](source/SM_API_USD/inc/SmApiUsd.h):** reads `BrepArray` prims into
  SMLib BReps and writes SMLib BReps back to USD.
- **[USD Validator](tools/brep_validator/README.md):** checks that the BReps in a USD file comply with the BRep
  schema.
- **[Healer](source/SM_API_USD/inc/SmApiUsdHeal.h):** heals the BReps across a whole USD scene, preserving layers,
  references, instancing, transforms and materials.
- **[Geometry validator](tools/brep_geometry_validator/README.md):** runs AssertValid (see [Kernel](#kernel)) on every
  `BrepArray` prim in a USD file.
- **[Tessellator](source/SM_API_USD/inc/SmApiUsdTessellate.h):** writes a `UsdGeomMesh` for each BRep in the `BrepArray`
  prims of a USD file.
- **Viewers:**
  - **[hdUsdBrep](source/HYDRA_USD_BREP/README.md):** Hydra plugin for viewing USD BReps in usdview.
  - **[view_usd](tools/scripts/view_usd.py):** shows a USD file's BReps, tessellated, in a PyVista window.
  - **[smlib_gui](tools/smlib_gui/README.md):** desktop app for opening, inspecting and editing USD and SMLib BReps.
- **Converters:**
  - **OpenCASCADE:** [occt_to_usd](tools/occt_to_usd/README.md) and [usd_to_occt](tools/usd_to_occt/README.md)
    convert between OpenCASCADE and USD BReps.
  - **Utility libraries:** [BREP_USD_DATA](source/BREP_USD_DATA/README.md),
    [BREP_STAGING](source/BREP_STAGING/README.md) and [USD_BREP_UTILS](source/USD_BREP_UTILS/README.md)
    support writing USD converters to and from other formats.
- **APIs:** [C++](source/SM_API_USD) and [Python](tools/pyproject/README.md) (USD).

### Kernel

The SMLib kernel, and tools that work on BReps in memory:

- **[Kernel (SMLib)](source/SMLib):** creates and edits BRep solids, with booleans, fillets,
  sweeps and offsets.
- **[Healer](source/SM_API/inc/SmApiHeal.h):** fixes common geometric and topological defects in BReps.
- **[Tessellator](source/SMLib/inc/SmTess.h):** meshes BReps into triangles. The Hydra plugin uses it to draw
  BReps in usdview.
- **Geometry validator (AssertValid):** checks the geometric quality and topological
  consistency of BReps in memory.
- **APIs:** [C++](source/SM_API) and [Python](tools/pyproject/README.md) (SMLib).
- **[Examples](Examples/README.md):** runnable Python and C++ examples for each API layer.

### Agents

Guidance for coding agents, starting from [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md):

- **[Docs](.agents/docs/OVERVIEW.md):** the library's layers and key concepts, what each
  error code means and how to fix it.
- **[Operations](.agents/operations/INDEX.md):** a guide for each API area, such as booleans,
  fillets, tessellation, healing and USD import/export.
- **[Skills](.agents/skills):** workflows for debugging kernel operations, using and
  maintaining the C++ and Python APIs, working with the USD schema and converters, choosing
  tests and writing bug reports.

## Documentation

[nvidia-omniverse.github.io/usd-brep](https://nvidia-omniverse.github.io/usd-brep/), including the Python and C++ API reference.

## Quick start

The Python package is on PyPI for CPython 3.12 on Linux (x86_64, aarch64) and Windows:

```bash
pip install usd-brep
```

```python
import usd_brep

sphere = usd_brep.primitives.create_sphere((0.0, 0.0, 0.0), 1.0)
box = usd_brep.primitives.create_box((0.0, 0.0, 0.0), 1.0, 1.0, 1.0)
cut = usd_brep.booleans.boolean_difference(sphere, box)  # a sphere missing one octant

usd_brep.usd.export_brep(cut, "cut.usda")
(brep,) = usd_brep.usd.import_breps("cut.usda")
```

To repair the BReps in an existing USD scene, `usd.heal_file` heals the `BrepArray`
geometry in the layers the scene uses and writes the scene with its layers,
references, instancing, transforms and materials kept:

```python
usd_brep.usd.heal_file("input.usdc", "input_healed.usdc")
```

See the [package README](tools/pyproject/README.md) for the API's submodules and
[Examples](Examples/README.md) for runnable examples in Python and C++.

# Shadow of the Colossus — PC native port · v0.60.6

[Releases](../../releases) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md)

> **No game or Sony files are included.** You need your own game dump and, for sound, two
> modules from your own console. This project is not affiliated with Sony Interactive
> Entertainment or Bluepoint Games.

---

**Status: the game can be finished from start to end** (v0.60.3: played through the last
colossus, the ending and the credits, with high quality textures, PS4 Pro mode and 60 FPS on).

A native Windows port of the PS4 **Shadow of the Colossus** (Bluepoint, 2018; CUSA08809, EU 1.01)
for **Windows 10/11**. The game's own x86-64 code runs directly on the PC's CPU and the PS4 GPU
is translated to Vulkan. It is not a full emulator: it is a loader with the system functions the
game needs, in the style of [bloodborne_pc](https://github.com/Supermedo/bloodborne_pc).

### What's new

| Version | Improvements and fixes |
|---|---|
| **0.60.6** | **No more rainbow garbage on textures and far fewer "closed out of nowhere" crashes** (the cause: speculative GPU readbacks written over memory the game had reused, after loading a save or a new area), **no more black dots on sandy ground**, **in-game menu cleaned up** (FPS, upscaler and sharpening now change at once; Bloodborne leftovers removed), **hard disk read-ahead** (fewer stalls in new areas on HDDs), textures refreshed on every load, a readable session event log (`user/events.log`). |
| **0.60.5** | **Texture quality selector: Off / High / Maximum** (#235: sharp again), **memory leak fixed** (~60 MB/min, long-session stutter), **+3% average and +12% minimum FPS** (descriptor binds reused), **loading after a GPU driver update: 106 s → 7 s**, possible fix for **white characters on AMD GCN** (RX 470–590, Vega), **4-thread CPUs** no longer stuck loading, a hang watchdog, short hitches no longer flash a black loading screen, code review fixes. |

# ReSkate

play it offline, host your own lobbies and dedicated servers, and mod it.
the launcher, the runtime that loads into the game, and the dedicated server.

> ReSkate is a fan project. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Electronic Arts or Full Circle.
> You need your own copy of skate. on Steam.

## Features

- **Offline play.** No EA servers needed. Your skater, outfits, unlocks and progress are saved on your PC,
  and the game runs even with Steam closed.
- **Multiplayer.**
  - Host a Steam lobby for up to 32 players: public, or joined with a code, with an optional password.
  - Join dedicated servers from the in-game server browser.
  - Proximity voice chat, and text chat with emotes and an optional bad-word filter.
  - Parties in lobbies and on dedicated servers: invite, join, leave, promote.
  - Throwdowns with other players (Jam, Spot Battle and S.K.A.T.E.), and co-op challenges. Plugins add
    throwdown modes of their own to the Throwdowns page ([contrib/throwdown-kit.md](contrib/throwdown-kit.md)).
- **In-game menu and console.**
  - Map and fast travel.
  - World: time of day, population, district levels, rotating parks.
  - The **Park Editor**: place, move and save objects with freecam, snapping and undo. Save a selection as a
    set and place it again anywhere, on any map.
  - Skater options: first person, movement, boosts, noclip.
  - Hall of Meat, grind exit triggers, Board Break, Road Rash and the FPV drone are plugin mods now,
    installed like any other mod. Board Break and Road Rash ship inside their asset mods.
  - Progression, controls, graphics and multiplayer settings.
- **Mods.**
  - Drop a mod in `Mods/` and it is merged into the game at launch. Mods can add custom maps, loading
    screens, cosmetics and scripts.
  - Browse and install mods from the [Thunderstore community](https://thunderstore.io/c/reskate/) in the
    launcher. A mod that needs others (a mod pack) brings them with it.
  - Save sets of mods as profiles, switch between them, and share one as a code or a file.
  - Most mod changes apply in game without a restart.
- **Launcher.**
  - Checks that you have the supported game build, and can download exactly that build with your Steam
    account.
  - Keeps ReSkate itself up to date.

## Getting started

1. Download the latest `ReSkate-<version>.zip` from
   [Releases](https://github.com/Dingo-Shenanigans/ReSkate/releases).
2. Extract `ReSkateLauncher.exe` and `ReSkate.dll` into **a new, empty folder of their own**, for
   example `C:\Games\ReSkate`. Do **not** put them in Steam's skate. folder: ReSkate keeps its own
   copy of the game there, so Steam updating skate. cannot break it.
3. Run `ReSkateLauncher.exe`.
   - It checks for ReSkate updates, then installs the supported build of the game into that folder
     (about 14 GB of free space).
   - Sign in to Steam when asked, with the account that owns skate. You can scan a QR code with the
     Steam app, or use your username and password with Steam Guard.
   - On later runs it checks the game files and downloads only what is missing.
4. Press **PLAY**.

ReSkate supports one game build at a time (Steam build `25414733`).

### Linux (Proton)

1. Install skate. with Steam, and put `ReSkateLauncher.exe` and `ReSkate.dll` in a new, empty folder
   of their own, for example `~/Games/ReSkate` (not Steam's skate. folder: the launcher refuses to
   run from there).
2. In Steam → skate. → Properties → Launch Options, enter this with your own folder's path:

   ```
   bash -c 'exec "${@/*EAAntiCheat.GameServiceLauncher.exe//home/you/Games/ReSkate/ReSkateLauncher.exe}"' -- %command%
   ```

3. Press **Play** on skate. in your Steam library. The launcher installs its own copy of the game
   into that folder the first time.

Steam starts EA's anti-cheat launcher (`EAAntiCheat.GameServiceLauncher.exe`), not `Skate.exe`, and the
anti-cheat refuses to run under Proton (*E111000B … Wine, Proton, and Steam Deck are not supported*).
The launch option swaps it for ReSkate's launcher, which starts the game itself. Launching from the game's
own Steam entry, rather than adding the launcher as a non-Steam game, keeps skate.'s app ID and its
Proton prefix.

The launcher in a folder of its own is new and has not been tested on Proton yet. With the launcher
beside `Skate.exe`, as it was set up before, ReSkate 1.1.3 was tested with Proton Experimental on
CachyOS: the launcher, the server browser, joining a public server and hosting a lobby. Steam Deck should work the same way but is untested. If you load a
custom map and then join a server on another map, the screen can stay black

# PS2 Web Recomp PlayStation 2 games running in the browser through static recompilation. The game's Emotion Engine machine code is translated ahead of time into C++ and compiled to WebAssembly, so the main CPU is never interpreted; the rest of the console, its operating system and hardware, is emulated by a runtime that draws with WebGPU.


Watch the full recording (1:24)

This is the sibling of [psp-web-recomp](https://github.com/snuri00/psp-web-recomp) and follows the same method. The first title brought up this way is Gran Turismo 4, chosen because it is one of the most demanding games on the system: it leans on both vector units, on exact floating point behaviour for its replays and license tests, and on graphics tricks that read rendered images back as palettes. It plays from boot through the opening movie, the menus and races, with music and sound effects, and saves to a memory card kept in the browser. A race runs at full speed, 50 frames per second for this PAL release, in Chrome on a laptop's integrated GPU at twice the PS2's resolution, which is how the recording above was made. God of War II followed through the same scripts. It needed no game-specific code, but it found two bugs that Gran Turismo 4 had never triggered, one in the recompiler and one in the vector unit timing, and a few missing pieces of the PS2's input/output processor. It now plays from the menus through its cutscenes into combat, and holds 60 frames per second in heavy combat at the PS2's resolution in Chrome. At twice the resolution it runs at 48 to 60, limited by the laptop's integrated GPU. No game data is included here. You bring a disc image of a game you own, and the scripts in this repository turn it into a web page on your machine. ## How it works **Recompilation.** `eerecomp` reads the game's executable, follows its control flow to find the functions and emits C++ for them in units of 16 KiB of guest code. The output keeps the R5900's quirks: 128-bit registers and the multimedia instructions that work on them, branch delay slots, the PS2's floating point unit, which has no infinities or denormals and rounds differently from IEEE, and vector unit 0 used as a coprocessor. Jumps between units become tail calls, and a thread switch unwinds the host stack and resumes at the guest address, so the generated code never needs a stack per guest thread. **A small PS2 kernel.** The EE side of the operating system is answered by high-level emulation: threads, semaphores, interrupt handlers for the DMA controller and the vertical blank, alarms, and the SIF channel that connects the main CPU to the I/O processor. The I/O processor runs the game's own IRX modules, the sound driver, the disc streaming code and the controller and memory card drivers that ship on the disc, on an interpreter of its R3000 CPU, while the IOP kernel and the libraries those modules call are reimplemented in C++. The disc is read over HTTP Range requests, so only the executable is downloaded up front. **Vector units.** Most of a PS2 game's 3D work happens in microprograms the game uploads to vector unit 1. They run with the pipeline delays of the MAC, status and clip flags modelled, because games schedule their code around them, and with the PS2's float rules for special values: no infinities or NaNs, denormals flushed to zero and overflow clamped to the largest float. The arithmetic itself is the host's, so a result can differ from the console's in its last bit; the console truncates where the host rounds, and its multiplier is not exact. Microprograms seen during a test run are compiled ahead of time into SIMD C++; any the page meets for the first time are translated into a WebAssembly module on the spot, which takes a few milliseconds per program. **Graphics.** The Graphics Synthesizer's 4 MB of video memory lives on the GPU, in its native swizzled layouts, and drawing is done by WebGPU compute shaders: triangles are binned into tiles and rasterized with the GS's own rules for texturing, palettes, alpha blending, depth and destination alpha tests. Because everything stays in GS memory, effects that render into a texture or reinterpret a framebuffer as a palette work the way they do on the console. The internal resolution can be one, two or three times the native one. A software rasterizer of the same GS remains as the reference the GPU output is compared against. **Threads.** The emulation runs in a worker, vector unit 1 has a worker of its own the way it runs in parallel on the console, and the GS commands go through a ring buffer to the page thread, which owns the WebGPU device. **Sound and movies.** The SPU2 is reimplemented with its 48 voices of ADPCM, ADSR envelopes and the streaming DMA games use for music, and its output goes to an AudioWorklet through shared memory. # SkyCraft

![SkyCraft: a Minecraft player walking through Riverwood with the Minecraft HUD](docs/screenshot.jpg)

Play Skyrim as a Minecraft player. You move with Minecraft's physics, carry Minecraft's inventory
and HUD, and place and break blocks in Skyrim's world. You fight Skyrim's NPCs with Minecraft
weapons, and they fight back.

Neither game is rewritten. Minecraft runs its own game logic, and Skyrim runs its world, NPCs,
quests and saves. A Skyrim SKSE plugin and a Minecraft Fabric mod talk to each other through
shared memory. Minecraft runs hidden in the background, and Skyrim draws everything.

> **Status: early and experimental.** Expect rough edges, and back up your saves.
> This is a fan project. It isn't affiliated with Mojang, Microsoft, Bethesda or ZeniMax, and you
> need to own both games.

## What works

- **Movement:** Minecraft movement on Skyrim's terrain and buildings. That covers walking,
  sprinting, jumping, crouching, swimming and falling, and Skyrim's collision is fed into
  Minecraft's own collision.
- **Blocks:** place and break blocks anywhere in Skyrim. They're drawn inside Skyrim's frame
  with its sun, shadows, fog and weather. Minecraft lights (torches, lava, glowstone and so on)
  light up Skyrim.
- **Digging into Skyrim:** mine Skyrim's ground, rocks, roads and objects like Minecraft blocks.
  What you dig out drops as the block it's made of (dirt under grass, then stone with ores, then
  bedrock), and the hole is real for you, NPCs and items. TNT, creepers and other explosions blow
  craters into Skyrim. Interiors and caves are solid stone behind their walls. What you dig is
  saved in your Minecraft world. **Skyrim destruction: On/Off** in the top left of the pause menu
  (O) turns it off (holes already dug stay).
- **Block entities:** chests, beds, banners, heads, shulker boxes and similar blocks are drawn,
  and pistons move blocks.
- **Water and lava:** they flow over Skyrim's terrain, and Skyrim water swims like Minecraft
  water.
- **Combat:** hit Skyrim NPCs with any Minecraft weapon, including bows, tridents and TNT.
  Damage is scaled to NPC level, and NPCs fight back.
  - NPCs collide with blocks and path around them.
  - Lava and fire hurt NPCs, and NPCs press pressure plates.
- **Skyrim progression:**
  - Your Skyrim skills level up from Minecraft play. Swords, maces and tools train
    One-Handed; axes and spears train Two-Handed; bows and anything thrown train Archery.
  - Shields train Block, and hits taken train Light or Heavy Armor depending on what you wear.
  - Crafting gear trains Smithing, and crouching is Skyrim sneak, which trains Sneak.
- **Camera and death:** Minecraft's F5 camera modes show your skin and armor in Skyrim. Dying
  gives Skyrim's death camera with your Minecraft body ragdolling.
- **Skyrim's own animations:** chairs, crafting stations, beds, pull levers, horses and scripted
  scenes hand control to Skyrim until they finish.
- **Multiplayer (Minecraft side only):** friends who also run SkyCraft can join your Minecraft
  world over the internet (see [Playing with friends](#playing-with-friends)).

## Requirements

**Skyrim**

| | |
|---|---|
| Skyrim Special Edition, **Anniversary Edition runtime** (1.6.x / 1.7.x) | Developed and tested on **1.7.104**. Not SE 1.5.97, not VR. |
| [SKSE64](https://skse.silverlock.org/) | For your game version |
| [Address Library for SKSE Plugins](https://www.nexusmods.com/skyrimspecialedition/mods/32444) | The "All in one (Anniversary Edition)" file |

> **Heavily recommended: [Alternate Start - Live Another Life](https://www.nexusmods.com/skyrimspecialedition/mods/272).**
> Skyrim's opening (the cart ride and Helgen) is heavily scripted and may not work with SkyCraft,
> so you can get stuck. Alternate Start skips it and lets you choose where your new character
> begins. Otherwise, play from a save made after Helgen.

**Minecraft**

You only need **a Microsoft account that owns Minecraft: Java Edition**. SkyCraft comes with
everything else: a portable [Prism Launcher](https://prismlauncher.org/) set up with Minecraft 26.3,
[Fabric](https://fabricmc.net/), [Fabric API](https://modrinth.com/mod/fabric-api) and the SkyCraft
Minecraft mod. Prism downloads Minecraft and Java itself.

Minecraft runs hidden next to Skyrim. Budget about 3 GB of extra RAM, about 1.5 GB of disk for
Minecraft's own files, and a GPU that runs Minecraft 26.3.

## Installing

1. **Install `SkyCraft-<version>.zip`** with Mod Organizer 2 or Vortex, like any SKSE plugin.
2. **Start Skyrim through SKSE.** The first time, SkyCraft unpacks its Minecraft to
   `%LOCALAPPDATA%\SkyCraft` and a small **Prism Launcher** window asks you to sign in with your
   Microsoft account. Alt-Tab to it, sign in, then go back to Skyrim. Prism downloads Minecraft,
   Fabric and Java (a few minutes, first time only), and Skyrim's corner messages tell you when
   Minecraft is ready.
3. **After that it's automatic.** Minecraft starts with Skyrim with no wind

# The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker HD — native port (macOS, Linux, Windows, Android)

A static recompilation of the Wii U version (USA or European) that runs natively on **macOS** (Apple Silicon),
**Linux**, **Windows** and **Android** (arm64; the setup app builds the game on the phone, see
[Android](#android-build-it-yourself)). The
game's PowerPC code is translated to C ahead of time, the Cafe OS libraries the game uses are
reimplemented natively, and GX2 graphics are implemented directly on Metal (macOS) or Vulkan (all
platforms), with no Cemu runtime and no GPU command emulation.

How it works and how it differs from running the game in Cemu: [docs/how-it-works.md](docs/how-it-works.md).

The project has three parts:
- **The port** (this repository): the recompiled game on macOS, Linux, Windows and Android, described below.
- **The decompilation** ([ZeldaWWHDDecomp/wwhd](https://github.com/ZeldaWWHDDecomp/wwhd)): readable C++ source
  for the game's code, each function tested against the original. The port can already run it in an
  experimental **decomp build**, the path towards a fully native source port; see
  [decomp build](#optional-decomp-build-experimental).
- **Mods** ([ZeldaWWHDRecomp/ZeldaWWHDMods](https://github.com/ZeldaWWHDRecomp/ZeldaWWHDMods)): built-in options
  and a catalogue of community mods, installed from inside the game; see [Mods](#mods).

## What's new

**v0.4.0: the world editor and a big Android update.**
- **World editor** (a preview for mod makers): start the game with `--editor` to place the game's villagers,
  enemies, chests, switches, doors and your own models while the game runs, and to build quests, letters, scenes,
  islands and levels of your own. It also works with AI assistants through MCP (off by default).
- **Android:** two-screen handhelds, a heat guard for handhelds with a fan, even frame pacing at 60 fps, code mods
  and dynamic resolution.
- **Faster on every platform**, a 40 fps mode, toon clouds, more comfort options and many fixes.

The changes in each update are in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) and in the release notes on the
[Releases](https://github.com/ZeldaWWHDRecomp/ZeldaWWHDRecomp/releases) page.

## Legal notice

This is an unofficial fan project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed or sponsored by Nintendo.
"The Legend of Zelda", "The Wind Waker", "Wii U" and related names are trademarks of their
respective owners and are used here only to describe what this software is compatible with.

This repository contains **no game code, no game assets and no keys**: no executable, no
recompiled or disassembled game code, no textures, models, audio, shaders, screenshots or other
material from the game, and no console encryption keys. It contains only the tools and the
runtime written for this project (plus the third-party code listed under Credits).

To use it you need your own, legally obtained copy of the game, dumped from your own Wii U disc
and console. Everything game-specific (the extracted files, the recompiled code in `build/gen/`,
shader caches) is generated locally on your machine from your dump, and must not be
redistributed. The `.gitignore` keeps all of it out of the repository.

## Install (releases)

Releases are portable: unzip, start **Wind Waker HD**, choose your dump. Releases contain only this
project's runtime, tools and setup: **no game files, no game code and no keys**. The game's code can
only exist once it is built from your own dump, so the first start prepares the game once, on your
computer (about two minutes); every later start launches the game directly.

1. Download the zip for your system from the
   [Releases](https://github.com/ZeldaWWHDRecomp/ZeldaWWHDRecomp/releases) page and unzip it anywhere
   (a games folder, an external drive):
   - **macOS**: Apple Silicon, macOS 14 or newer (Metal renderer; Vulkan through MoltenVK, included, can
     be picked in Graphics > Renderer)
   - **Windows**: x86-64 (`windows-x86_64`, Windows 10 version 1903 or newer, or Windows 11) or arm64 (`windows-arm64`, Windows 11 on
     ARM, e.g. Snapdragon X), a GPU with Vulkan 1.3 drivers (or Vulkan 1.1 / 1.2 drivers with
     `VK_KHR_dynamic_rendering`). The arm64 zip runs natively, and only on ARM64 (its setup says so
     on an x86-64 PC). On ARM, 60 fps keeps the game's speed by default (Graphics > "Keep game
     speed"), as on Android: where two frames per step do not fit, in-between frames are skipped
     instead of slowing the whole game down
   - **Linux**: x86-64 (`linux-x86_64`) or arm64 (`linux-aarch64`, e.g. Raspberry Pi 5, Asahi Linux
     on Apple Silicon, other ARM boards and laptops), glibc 2.35 or newer (Ubuntu 22.04+, Debian 12+,
     Fedora 36+, Arch, SteamOS 3, Raspberry Pi OS 12), a GPU with Vulkan 1.3 drivers (or 1.1 / 1.2 with
     `VK_KHR_dynamic_rendering`). Take the zip
     that matches `uname -m` (`x86_64` or `aarch64`); setup says so if it doesn't. Or take the
     single-file **AppImage** (same two architectures)

# bbhost

bbhost is a translation layer that runs Bloodborne on Windows and Linux. The
game's own 1.09 executable runs unmodified on the PC's x86-64 CPU; bbhost
answers its calls into the PS4's system libraries with PC implementations, and
recompiles its GPU work, GCN shaders and the engine's draw calls, for Vulkan.
The aim is a definitive PC version of the game - the original, intact, with
what a PC release would add: any resolution and aspect ratio, 60 fps and
beyond, keyboard and mouse, proper settings, mods and online play.

![Cainhurst Castle](docs/images/cainhurst.jpg)

bbhost contains no game code or data. You need your own copy of the game: a
dump with the 1.09 update and its decrypted executable.

## Why not emulation

The PS4 has an x86-64 CPU, so the game's code does not need to be translated
to run on a PC - it needs a place to live. bbhost provides that place:

- **The CPU side runs natively.** bbhost loads the game's ELF executable,
  relocates it, links its imports to its own implementations and starts it.
  The game's code runs at full speed on the host CPU, with no interpreter or
  recompiler involved.
- **The PS4's system libraries are reimplemented** for the PC: files and
  saves, threads and memory, input, audio, movies, networking and the
  PlayStation Network calls the online features use - every one of the 660
  named functions the game imports.
- **Graphics are being moved from emulation to native code.** The game's
  renderer was written for the PS4's GPU: it builds command buffers for an AMD
  GCN GPU and ships GCN shader programs. bbhost hooks FromSoftware's own
  graphics layer instead, so draws, dispatches, clears and copies are built
  directly from the engine's objects, and decompiles the shaders to typed,
  structured SPIR-V, which it prints as HLSL for the player's PC to compile.
  The status table below shows what is native today and what the GPU command
  processor still emulates.
- **Game functions are being rewritten as source**, one at a time, each checked
  against the original, so the game can be fixed and extended where a patch
  would not reach.

## Features

| | |
|---|---|
| ![Yharnam in 21:9](docs/images/yharnam-ultrawide.jpg) | **Any resolution, ultrawide included.** 21:9 and 32:9 with a wider field of view and the HUD where it belongs, and the resolution can be changed while playing. FSR 1 upscaling for slower GPUs. |
| ![PC Graphics settings](docs/images/pc-graphics.jpg) | **Settings in the game's own menus.** The System menu gains PC Settings, PC Graphics, PC Effects, PC Controls, PC Camera and Key Bindings, drawn in the game's style: anti-aliasing, ambient occlusion, shadow distance, fog, motion blur, field of view, frame rate and more. |

- **60 fps and beyond**: 30, 60, 90, 120 or uncapped, with the game's timing
  corrected so physics, animation and cutscenes run at the right speed at each,
  and its effects keeping the pace they have at 30 while they move smoothly.
- **Keyboard and mouse**: mouse camera, a pointer in every menu, rebindable
  keys, and button prompts that show the keys.
- **PC enhancements** that can be switched off for the game as it shipped: the
  Hunter's Dream mirror opens the character appearance editor (a feature cut
  from the release), "Rebirth in the Nightmare" at the Altar of
  Despair lets you redistribute your levels, and the late areas allow two
  invaders, as the chalice dungeons do.
- **Online play** through a private server: co-op, invasions, messages,
  bloodstains and summon signs between bbhost players.
- **Mods** without touching the game files: replacement files, param tables
  edited by field name, byte patches as data (the community's among them, each
  with a switch in the setup window), and native plugins - a
  randomizer (items, shops and enemies), a boss rush, gameplay mutators and
  the developers' own debug menu ship with it.
- **A setup window** that finds and checks your game files, and the Steam Deck
  as a supported device.

![The setup window](docs/images/setup-window.png)

## Status

The game is playable on Windows and Linux: the world, its bosses and online
sessions. What runs on native code and what is still emulated:

| Part | State |
|---|---|
| Game logic (CPU) | the game's own code, running natively |
| System libraries | reimplemented by bbhost: all 660 named imports the game binds |
| Window, input, audio, movies, saves | native (SDL3, Vulkan, FFmpeg, LibAtrac9) |
| Online | native sockets and HTTP against a private server; peer-to-peer UDP with NAT traversal |
| Draws | native: each draw is built from the engine's graphics objects; the command buffer only marks its place in the stream |
| Post-processing (YEBIS) | native: every stage's resources built by bbhost |
| Tessellation | native: the host GPU's own tessellation stages, all three stages lifted; the game's mesh hulls draw as one native pipeline, without the PS4's on-chip ring |
| Shaders | decompiled ("lifted") from GCN to typed, structure

# DeepGEMM Ascend

DeepGEMM Ascend is a port of DeepGEMM to the HUAWEI Ascend platform. It is fully API-compatible with DeepGEMM and supports BF16, FP8, FP4 GEMM, MQA logits, and MegaMoE. On Ascend platforms, users can simply install the package and use the same APIs and development workflow as DeepGEMM on other supported platforms.

DeepGEMM Ascend provides a lightweight abstraction over the Ascend MAD (matrix multiply-add) primitives, hiding much of the complexity associated with fractal layouts, alignment constraints, address calculations, and verbose low-level parameters. This enables GEMM kernels to remain both concise and efficient. DeepGEMM Ascend makes extensive use of Ascend-specific optimization techniques, such as sparse data loading and coroutine-based pipelining, to approach the performance limits of the Ascend hardware. These implementations can also serve as references for extreme performance optimization on the Ascend platform.

Despite its lightweight codebase, DeepGEMM Ascend can achieve peak hardware performance across a wide range of matrix shapes.

DeepGEMM Ascend 是华为昇腾平台上的 DeepGEMM 实现。它完全兼容 DeepGEMM 的 API，支持 BF16、FP8、FP4 GEMM、MQA logits 和 MegaMoE 算子。DeepGEMM Ascend 和 DeepGEMM 使用相同的包名，用户只需安装当前包，即可沿用其他平台上 DeepGEMM 的 API 和开发流程。

DeepGEMM Ascend 对昇腾平台的矩阵乘加原语（MAD）提供了一个轻量的抽象，能够隐藏分形矩阵布局、对齐约束、地址计算、参数转换等细节，让 GEMM kernel 的实现保持简洁高效。DeepGEMM Ascend 广泛采用昇腾平台特有的优化技术，包括稀疏数据加载、基于协程的流水线等，以接近硬件的性能极限。这些实现也可以作为昇腾平台极致性能优化的参考。

DeepGEMM Ascend 代码轻量，并且在多种矩阵形状上能达到硬件极限性能。

## News

- 2026.09.30: Initial release of DeepGEMM Ascend, with support for Ascend 950 devices. The kernels are designed to achieve near-peak hardware performance.

## Quick Start

### Requirements

- HUAWEI Ascend NPU (developed and validated on the Ascend 950 series)
- CANN 9.20 toolkit providing `bin/bisheng`, `bin/ld.lld`
- Torch NPU package `torch_npu`
- Python 3.10 or higher
- Compilers and standard libraries with C++20 `<format>` support
- `tilelang`, used by the HC prenorm kernel (declared as a package dependency)
- `tree-sitter` and `tree-sitter-cpp`, used to generate Python type stubs when building from source

### Development

```bash
# Submodule must be cloned
git clone --recursive https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM-Ascend.git
cd DeepGEMM-Ascend

# Link some essential includes and build the C++ extension
cat develop.sh
./develop.sh
```

### Installation

```bash
pip install . --no-build-isolation
```

## Interfaces

### Kernel Interface

Please refer to [DeepGEMM's interfaces](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM#interfaces) for the kernel APIs.

> [!NOTE]
> The scaling factor format on Ascend differs from NVIDIA's: each pair of UE8M0 scaling factors along the K dimension is packed into an `int16`, and the packed values are stored in MN-major order for optimal hardware efficiency.

Dense BF16, FP8, FP4 and mixed FP8×FP4 GEMMs accept `c` with shape `[M, N]` or `[1, N]`
and the same dtype as `d`. Full C uses atomic add. A contiguous `[1, N]` bias is loaded
and added in the AIV epilogue before the output cast.
The `bf16_gemm_nn` and `fp8_fp4_gemm_nn` interfaces take `A[M, K]` and `B[K, N]`:

```python
deep_gemm.bf16_gemm_nn(a, b, c=bias, d=d)
```

### Utilities

The library provides some utility functions besides the above kernels:

- `deep_gemm.set_num_sms` / `get_num_sms`: set/get the number of AI cores the kernels may use
- `deep_gemm.set_npu_arch` / `get_npu_arch`: override/query the `dav-*` NPU architecture used for JIT compilation, `0` queries the device
- `deep_gemm.set_mk_alignment_for_contiguous_layout` / `get_mk_alignment_for_contiguous_layout`: set/get the group-level M/K alignment for contiguous layout
- `deep_gemm.get_theoretical_mk_alignment_for_contiguous_layout`: get the theoretical minimum M/K alignment
- `deep_gemm.use_deterministic_algorithms` / `get_deterministic_algorithms`: enable/disable deterministic algorithms
- `deep_gemm.transform_sf_into_required_layout`: transform scaling factors into the required layout
- `deep_gemm.transform_k_grouped_sf_into_required_layout`: transform K-grouped scaling factors into the required layout
- `deep_gemm.get_paged_mqa_logits_metadata`: build the scheduling metadata for the paged MQA kernels
- `deep_gemm.aclnn_fp8_fp4_gemm_{nt, nn, tn, tt}` and `deep_gemm.aclnn_bf16_gemm_{nt, nn, tn, tt}`: ACLNN reference GEMMs used to cross-check the kernels in tests

### Environment Variables

Ascend home path is given by `ASCEND_HOME_PATH` or `ASCEND_TOOLKIT_HOME`.

Each `DG_JIT_*` variable falls back to the corresponding global `DJ_JIT_*` variable when unset, and is snapshotted when the JIT runtime is first created.
